book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 4 · Medical and Legal Issues
title: Negligence, Consent, Refusal and the PCR
next: Chapter 5, Lesson 1: Ethics on the job: autonomy, end of life and accountability

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already ask permission, handle refusals and write PCRs. As a PCP, the treatments behind each yes or no get bigger:

  1. The four elements of negligence, and avoiding abandonment
  2. Consent, capacity and refusal, step by step
  3. Restraint, crime scenes, and a PCR that protects you

Textbook: Chapter 4, PDF pages 243–275
slides.say: Welcome back. As an EMR, you already ask before you treat, you've met patients who say no, and you write a PCR on every call. Now that you're practising as a PCP, the treatments behind each yes or no are bigger: needles, fluids and more drugs. That makes consent, refusal and documentation weigh more. Today we'll cover what a patient must prove to win a negligence case, and how to avoid abandonment; consent, decision-making capacity and refusal, step by step; and finally restraint, crime scenes, and a PCR that protects you and your patient.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你已经会在治疗前征得同意，也遇到过说「不」的病人，每次出车都写 PCR。现在以 PCP 身份执业，每一个「同意」或「拒绝」背后的治疗更大了：打针、补液、更多的药。所以同意、拒绝和记录的分量更重。今天讲：病人要证明什么才能打赢过失官司，以及如何避免遗弃；同意、决策能力和拒绝，一步一步来；最后是约束、犯罪现场，以及一份能保护你和病人的 PCR。

slides.title: Negligence: four links in a chain
slides.body:
Duty→Breach→Proximate cause→Harm
  • The patient must prove all four
  • Breach by omission (less than trained) or commission (beyond training)
  • Foreseeable harm should be prevented, like a wrong drug dose
  • On the job, ordinary negligence is enough to lose

Proximate cause is the hardest link: record findings at first contact.
slides.say: To win a negligence case, the patient must prove four links. Duty: you had a legal duty to care for them. Breach: you fell below the standard of care, by omission, doing less than your training requires, like skipping a blood sugar on a confused diabetic, or by commission, doing more than your training allows. Proximate cause: your breach directly caused the injury. Harm: damage resulted. Foreseeable harm, like a wrong drug dose, should be prevented, and on the job even a simple mistake can be enough. Proximate cause is the hardest to prove, so record the patient's condition at first contact.
slides.sayZh: 要打赢过失官司，病人必须证明四个环节。职责：你对他负有法定照护职责。违反职责：你的处置低于照护标准，可能是不作为，也就是做得少于训练要求，比如对意识混乱的糖尿病人不测血糖；也可能是作为错误，做了超出训练范围的事。近因：你的违反直接造成了伤害。损害：确实有损害发生。可预见的伤害应当预防，比如给错药物剂量；工作中，哪怕一个简单失误也可能足以败诉。近因最难证明，所以要记录你初次接触病人时的状况。

slides.title: Abandonment and a proper handover
slides.body:
Care ends only when a qualified person takes over

  • Hand over only to equal or higher training
  • Give a full report to a physician, PA or nurse
  • Waiting room only if staff agree and accept the patient
  • Always leave a copy of your PCR
slides.say: Abandonment is ending care without the patient's agreement while they still need it, and harm follows. Once you've started, stay until a qualified professional with equal or higher training accepts the patient; a clerk or an empty stretcher doesn't count. At a busy emergency department, give a full report to a physician, physician assistant or nurse. A stable patient may go to the waiting room only if staff agree and clearly accept responsibility. Always leave a copy of your PCR. For a PCP, "equal or higher" matters: a patient who needs ongoing PCP-level care can't simply go to a less-trained crew.
slides.sayZh: 遗弃是在病人仍需要照护时，未经他同意就终止照护，结果造成伤害。一旦开始照护，就要守到一名同级或更高级别的合格医护人员接手；文员或一张空担架都不算。在繁忙的急诊科，要向医生、医师助理或护士完整报告。病情稳定的病人，只有在医护人员同意并明确接手后，才可以去候诊区。一定要留下 PCR 副本。对 PCP 来说，「同级或更高」很关键：仍需要 PCP 级别持续照护的病人，不能随便交给训练更少的团队。

slides.title: Valid consent: four requirements
slides.body:
• Voluntary
  • Given with legal and mental capacity
  • Specific to the treatment and the provider
  • Informed
The problem→Treatment + risks→Alternatives→Risks of saying no

Ask, don't announce. Record how you got consent.
slides.say: Canadian common law gives every person the right to refuse any touching, even life-saving treatment, and the Constitution Act of nineteen eighty-two protects that right. So consent is valid only if it's voluntary, given with legal and mental capacity, specific to the treatment and the person giving it, and informed. To inform, explain in plain words what you think is wrong, the treatment and its risks, the alternatives, and what could happen if they say no. Consent can be spoken, or shown by action, like holding out an arm. Always ask rather than announce, even for a blood pressure, and record how you got consent.
slides.sayZh: 加拿大普通法赋予每个人拒绝任何触碰的权利，包括救命的治疗，Constitution Act（1982）保护这项权利。所以有效同意必须是：自愿的；由具有法律和心智能力的人作出；针对具体治疗和具体施治者；知情的。要做到知情，用浅白的话讲清：你认为是什么问题、治疗及其风险、替代方案、拒绝可能带来的后果。同意可以说出来，也可以用动作表示，比如伸出手臂。永远是「询问」而不是「通知」，哪怕只是量血压，并记录你是怎样取得同意的。

slides.q: A woman who is vomiting lets you take her vital signs and blood sugar. When you suggest an IV for fluids, she says, "No needles." She is alert and capable. What do you do?
options: Start the IV; she already agreed to your care
Respect her refusal of the IV, explain the risks and options, and document
Have her sign a refusal for the whole call and leave
Wait until she's too weak to object, then use implied consent
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A woman who is vomiting lets you take her vital signs and blood sugar. When you suggest an IV for fluids, she says, no needles. She's alert and capable. What do you do? A, start the IV; she already agreed to your care. B, respect her refusal of the IV, explain the risks and options, and document. C, have her sign a refusal for the whole call and leave. D, wait until she's too weak to object, then use implied consent. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位呕吐的女士让你测了生命体征和血糖。你建议开静脉补液时，她说：「不要打针。」她清醒、有决策能力。你怎么做？A 开静脉，她已经同意你的照护了；B 尊重她拒绝静脉，解释风险和其他选择，并记录；C 让她签一张整次出车的拒绝书然后离开；D 等她虚弱到无法反对时，按默示同意处理。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Consent is specific to each treatment, so yes to vital signs isn't yes to a needle. Explain the risks of going without the IV, keep giving the care she accepts, and document. A ignores that. C abandons care she still wants. D is wrong: implied consent can't override a refusal she made while capable.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。同意针对每一项具体治疗，同意测生命体征不等于同意扎针。解释不开静脉的风险，继续提供她接受的照护，并记录下来。A 忽略了这一点；C 放弃了她仍然想要的照护；D 错，她在有能力时作出的拒绝，不能用默示同意来推翻。

slides.title: When the patient can't consent
slides.body:
• Implied consent: unconscious or too ill to say, life at risk
  • Not if they refused that care while still capable
  • Adults are presumed capable; some provinces: from age 16
  • Mature minor: under 16 but fully understands → can decide
  • Child, or adult with a guardian: ask the parent or guardian

There's no such thing as "involuntary consent".
slides.say: What about patients who can't consent? An unconscious adult, or one too sick to communicate, is treated under implied consent: we assume they'd want life-saving care. But if you know they refused that care while capable, implied consent can't override it. Adults are presumed capable, and some provinces extend that from age sixteen. Below that, the mature minor rule lets a young person who fully understands the treatment and its consequences decide. For children, and adults with a guardian, ask the parent or guardian; if no one is available, life-saving care goes ahead. And legally, there's no such thing as involuntary consent.
slides.sayZh: 无法给出同意的病人怎么办？昏迷的成年人，或病重到无法沟通的人，按默示同意处理：我们推定他们想要救命的照护。但如果你知道他在有能力时拒绝过这项照护，默示同意就不能推翻这个拒绝。成年人推定有决策能力，有些省份从十六岁起就适用。更小的，按成熟未成年人规则，能充分理解治疗及其后果的年轻人可以自己决定。儿童，以及有监护人的成年人，要征求父母或监护人同意；找不到人时，救命处置照常进行。另外，法律上根本没有「非自愿同意」这回事。

slides.title: Decision-making capacity: the checklist
slides.body:
• Oriented to person, place and day; answers make sense
  • No major impairment from alcohol, drugs, head injury or illness
  • Can explain their condition and the risks of refusing
  • Has a reasonable follow-up plan
  • Normal SpO₂ and normal blood glucose

Altered mental status or unstable vital signs: probably can't refuse.
slides.say: Consent and refusal both rest on decision-making capacity: the ability to understand information, think it through, and make a choice that fits the patient's situation. Your best tool is conversation. Typical criteria: oriented to person, place and day, with sensible answers. No major impairment from alcohol, drugs, head injury or illness; ask family if this is normal for them. They can explain what's wrong and the risks of refusing. They have a sensible follow-up plan. And their oxygen saturation and blood glucose are normal, giving you objective numbers. Altered mental status or unstable vital signs usually means they can't refuse. Document it all.
slides.sayZh: 同意和拒绝都以决策能力为前提：能理解信息、想清楚，并作出符合自身情况的选择。最好的工具是交谈。常用标准：对人、地点、日期定向清楚，回答切题；没有酒精、药物、颅脑外伤或疾病造成的明显损害，可以问家属他平时是不是这样；能说出哪里不对、拒绝有什么风险；有合理的后续就医计划；血氧饱和度和血糖正常，给你客观数据。意识改变或生命体征不稳定，通常意味着不能拒绝。这些都要记录。

slides.title: When a capable patient says no
slides.body:
• No treatment without a court order: respect it
  • Find out why; explain the risks calmly
  • Call direct medical control; offer them the phone
  • Leave the door open: call back, follow-up, someone stays
  • Record: history, exam, mental status, reasons, advice, time spent
  • Signatures: patient + an impartial witness who heard it

A signature alone is not an informed refusal.
slides.say: If a capable patient refuses, you can't treat without a court order. Don't treat them as a bad patient; find out why. Fear and denial are common. Explain the risks calmly, call direct medical control, and let the patient talk to the physician if that helps. Some accept transport but not treatment, or the reverse. Leave the door open: they can call back any time, someone should stay with them, and they should see a doctor. Then document the history, exam, mental status, their reasons, your advice, and how long you tried. Get their signature, plus an impartial witness who actually heard the conversation.
slides.sayZh: 有决策能力的病人拒绝时，没有法院命令你就不能治疗。不要把他当成「难缠的病人」，先弄清原因，恐惧和否认很常见。冷静地解释风险，联系直接医疗指导，有帮助的话让病人直接和医生通话。有人同意转运但不同意治疗，也有人相反。把门留着：随时可以再打电话，最好有人陪着，并且要去看医生。然后记录病史、检查、精神状态、拒绝理由、你的建议，以及你劝说了多久。请病人签名，再请一位真的听到了对话的公正见证人签名。

slides.title: Doubtful capacity, force and restraint
slides.body:
• Capacity in doubt + possible life threat → lean toward transport
  • Consult medical control first; call police before restraining
  • Mental health, no life threat: forced transport is a police role
  • Force only in self-defence: equal or slightly greater
  • Restrain only for danger to self or others; never as punishment
  • Look for causes: hypoxia, low blood sugar, head injury, drugs

Safe restraint takes at least four trained people.
slides.say: If capacity is doubtful and the problem could be life-threatening, lean toward transport, even against the patient's wishes; wrongful detention is far less serious than a preventable death. But consult direct medical control first, and call police before you restrain anyone. For a mental health patient whose life isn't in danger, forced transport is usually a police role; in most regions, family or a doctor can't authorise it. Use force only to defend yourself, equal to or slightly more than the patient's. Restrain only when someone is in danger, never as punishment, and look for causes like hypoxia or low blood sugar.
slides.sayZh: 如果决策能力存疑，而问题可能危及生命，就倾向于送医，即使违背病人意愿；错误扣留的后果，远比一个本可避免的死亡轻。但要先咨询直接医疗指导，约束任何人之前先叫警察。精神科病人如果没有生命危险，强制转运通常是警察的职责，在大多数地区，家属或医生都无权授权。只能为自卫使用武力，力度等于或略大于病人的力度。只有在有人面临危险时才约束，绝不能当作惩罚；还要找原因，比如缺氧或低血糖。

slides.title: A PCR that protects you
slides.body:
• Times: call, arrival, leaving scene, at hospital
  • History, with direct quotes marked and attributed
  • Scene clues, full exam, pertinent negatives
  • Treatment exactly: who ordered, gauge, site, fluid, rate
  • Every change in the patient's condition
  • Facts only: no labels, no blaming colleagues

Not written = can't prove you did it. Leave a copy at the ED.
slides.say: Your best protection in court is a thorough, accurate record. You're the only one who saw the scene, so paint the picture for the hospital. Record the times: call, arrival, leaving the scene, arrival at hospital. Record the history, with direct quotes marked and attributed. Note scene clues, your full exam, and pertinent negatives, meaning things you checked that were normal or that the patient denied. Be exact about treatment: who ordered it, catheter size and site, fluid and rate. Note every change. Write it soon, facts only, with no labels or blame. If it isn't written, you can't prove you did it.
slides.sayZh: 法庭上最好的保护是一份详尽准确的记录。只有你见过现场，所以要替医院还原现场。记录时间：接警、到场、离开现场、到达医院。记录病史，直接引语要标明并注明是谁说的。写下现场线索、完整体检和相关阴性，也就是你查过但正常、或病人否认的情况。处置要写精确：谁下的医嘱、导管型号和部位、液体和速度。记录每一次变化。尽快写，只写事实，不贴标签、不指责。没写下来，就无法证明你做过。

slides.q: A 70-year-old man fell at home. He wants you to leave, but he thinks it's last week, and his SpO₂ is 87%. What's the best plan?
options: Get his signature on a refusal form and leave
He may lack capacity: keep assessing, call medical control, lean toward transport
Leave, because adults are presumed capable
Have a neighbour sign as a witness, then leave
slides.say: Here's a decision for you. A seventy-year-old man fell at home. He wants you to leave, but he thinks it's last week, and his oxygen saturation is eighty-seven percent. What's the best plan? A, get his signature on a refusal form and leave. B, he may lack capacity, so keep assessing, call medical control, and lean toward transport. C, leave, because adults are presumed capable. D, have a neighbour sign as a witness, then leave. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道决策题。一位七十岁男士在家摔倒。他要你走，但他以为现在是上周，血氧饱和度八十七。最好的方案是什么？A 让他在拒绝书上签字然后离开；B 他可能缺乏决策能力，所以继续评估、联系医疗指导、倾向于送医；C 离开，因为成年人推定有能力；D 请邻居签字作见证人，然后离开。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. He fails two capacity checks: he isn't oriented to the date, and his oxygen saturation is low. Keep assessing and treating, consult direct medical control, and lean toward transport. A is wrong: a signature doesn't make a refusal informed. C is wrong: clear evidence like this outweighs the presumption of capacity. D is wrong: a witness must actually hear the discussion, and capacity is still missing.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。他有两项能力标准不过关：日期定向不清，血氧偏低。要继续评估和处置，咨询直接医疗指导，并倾向于送医。A 错，签字不会让拒绝变成知情拒绝；C 错，这样明确的证据已经推翻了「推定有能力」；D 错，见证人必须真的听到对话，而且病人仍然缺乏能力。

slides.title: Crime scenes and reportable cases
slides.body:
• Touch only what you must; tell police what you moved
  • Keep clothing; don't cut through bullet or knife holes
  • Stay with a body until police arrive; if in doubt, resuscitate
  • Report suspected child and elder abuse (nearly every province)
  • Coroner: homicide, suicide, sudden unexpected death, inmate death
slides.say: At a possible crime scene, the patient comes first, but protect the evidence. Touch only what you must, avoid phones and door handles, and limit how many crew go in. If you move something, tell the police. Keep removed clothing, and don't cut through bullet or knife holes. At a death, stay with the body until police arrive, but if there's any chance of saving the patient, resuscitate. Reporting rules vary by province, yet nearly all require you to report suspected child or elder abuse. Generally, the coroner is told of homicides, suicides, other sudden or unexpected deaths, and deaths of prison inmates.
slides.sayZh: 在可能的犯罪现场，病人第一，但也要保护证据。只碰必须碰的东西，避开电话和门把手，限制进入的人数。挪动了东西要告诉警察。脱下的衣物要保留，不要剪穿弹孔或刀孔。遇到死亡，要守着遗体直到警察到达；但只要有救活的可能，就要复苏。各省的报告规定不同，但几乎都要求报告疑似虐待儿童或老人的情况。一般来说，凶杀、自杀、其他突发或意外死亡，以及囚犯死亡，都要通知验尸官。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Ask consent for each treatment: the IV, the fluid, each drug
  • Explain the risks of what you propose, in plain words
  • Combative? Think hypoxia or low sugar; you can treat the cause
  • Document exactly: order, gauge, site, fluid, rate, drug, dose, time
  • Hand PCP-level care only to equal or higher training
  • Your licence can be restricted, suspended or revoked
slides.say: Here's how this weighs more on a PCP. Consent is specific, so you'll ask more often: the IV, the fluid and each drug need their own informed yes, with the risks explained. With a combative patient, think hypoxia or low blood sugar; as a PCP you can now treat the cause. Document precisely: who ordered it, catheter size and site, fluid and rate, and every drug with its dose and time. Hand PCP-level care only to equal or higher training; if only basic care is needed, follow local protocol or ask medical control. And your licence can be restricted, suspended or revoked, with due process: notice and a hearing.
slides.sayZh: 下面说说这些为什么对 PCP 分量更重。同意是具体的，所以你要问的次数更多：静脉、补液、每一种药都需要各自的知情同意，并讲清风险。遇到攻击性强的病人，想想缺氧或低血糖；作为 PCP，你现在能治疗病因了。记录要精确：谁下的医嘱、导管型号和部位、液体和速度，以及每种药的剂量和时间。PCP 级别的照护只能交给同级或更高级别的人；如果只需要基础照护，按当地流程或请示医疗指导。还有，你的执照可以被限制、暂停或吊销，但享有正当程序：书面通知和听证。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Yes to vital signs is not yes to a needle
  • A capable "no" to an IV isn't erased later by implied consent
  • Errors of commission: any skill or drug outside your licence
  • Leaving a patient in the waiting room without staff accepting them
  • A signed refusal with no capacity assessment behind it
  • Labels like "drunk", or blaming a colleague, in your PCR
slides.say: Now the traps. First, consent doesn't carry over: a patient who let you check vital signs hasn't agreed to a needle. Second, if a capable patient refused an IV, you can't wait until they're too weak to object and call it implied consent. Third, errors of commission: any skill or drug outside your licence is a breach of duty. Fourth, a busy emergency department doesn't excuse abandonment; staff must accept your patient. Fifth, a signed refusal without a real capacity assessment won't protect you. And sixth, watch your words: labels and blame in a PCR can become libel.
slides.sayZh: 下面是陷阱。第一，同意不能延续：让你测生命体征的病人，并没有同意扎针。第二，有能力的病人拒绝了静脉，你不能等他虚弱到无力反对时再说是默示同意。第三，作为错误：任何超出你执照范围的技能或药物，都构成违反职责。第四，急诊科再忙也不能成为遗弃的借口，医护人员必须接手你的病人。第五，没有真正评估决策能力就签的拒绝书，保护不了你。第六，注意措辞：PCR 里的标签和指责可能构成书面诽谤。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Adult CPR: a verifiable DNR or No CPR order is a contraindication
  • Shown a valid DNR or No CPR order during CPR? You may stop
  • Benzodiazepines are not in BC EMR or PCP scope
  • Hypoglycemia: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L; PCP IV glucose is D10W only
  • EMRs have no IV access in BC

Book: a Canadian DNR is often valid only under the doctor or facility that wrote it.
slides.say: Now the BC rules. In the BC adult CPR protocol, a verifiable Do Not Resuscitate order, or No CPR order, is a contraindication to CPR, and if you're shown a valid one after starting, you may stop. A DNR isn't a do-not-care order. The book adds that a Canadian DNR is often valid only under the physician or facility that wrote it. The book also mentions calming drugs such as benzodiazepines for restraint; they are not in BC EMR or PCP scope. And if aggression comes from low sugar, BC treats a glucose under four point zero as hypoglycemia, and the PCP's IV glucose is D ten W only.
slides.sayZh: 下面是 BC 的规定。BC 成人 CPR 流程中，可核实的 DNR（不复苏）医嘱或 No CPR 医嘱是 CPR 的禁忌；如果开始后有人出示了有效的这类医嘱，你可以停止。DNR 不是「不照护」医嘱。书里还说，加拿大的 DNR 往往只在开具它的医生照护下或开具机构内有效。书里还提到约束时可用苯二氮卓类等镇静药，但它们不在 BC EMR 或 PCP 的执业范围内。如果攻击行为来自低血糖：BC 把血糖低于四点零按低血糖处理，PCP 的静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Negligence needs duty, breach, proximate cause and harm
  2. Consent, and refusal, must be voluntary, capable, specific and informed
  3. Your PCR is your defence: precise, factual, a copy left at the ED

Next: ethics on the job: autonomy, end of life and accountability
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: negligence needs all four links: duty, breach, proximate cause and harm. Avoid abandonment: hand over only to equal or higher training, with a full report and a copy of your PCR. Two: consent must be voluntary, capable, specific and informed, and so must a refusal; check capacity and document it. Three: your PCR is your defence, so make it precise, factual and timely. Next lesson moves from law to ethics: autonomy, substitute decision makers, end of life, and owning your mistakes. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，过失需要四个环节齐全：职责、违反、近因、损害。避免遗弃：只交给同级或更高级别的人，完整报告并留下 PCR 副本。二，同意必须自愿、有能力、具体、知情，拒绝也一样；评估决策能力并记录下来。三，PCR 是你的辩护，要精确、客观、及时。下节课从法律转到伦理：自主、替代决策者、临终，以及为自己的差错负责。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
